newsitem.title: POLAND: UNIVERSAL TO BID FOR ROMET BIKE MAKER.
newsitem.headline: UNIVERSAL TO BID FOR ROMET BIKE MAKER.

text.p: Polish trader Universal SA plans to bid for at least 10 percent of bicycle maker Romet SA, up to 80 percent of which is being offered by the treasury ministry, Universal's spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"We plan to submit a bid to buy no less than 10 percent of Romet's shares, but we don't know how many yet," Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters.
Last week the treasury ministry invited bids for Romet, whose full name is Zaklady Rowerowe Romet SA setting a deadline for April 7.
The ministry said 15 percent of shares would be earmarked for employees and five percent for restitution claims.
Romet, based in the central city of Bydgoszcz, employs 4,000 people.
Szostek also said Universal sought later this year to list 72.6-percent-owned condom maker Unimil Sp z o o on the Warsaw bourse's free market for small, less-liquid stocks.
She said Universal needed the consent of Unimil's minority shareholders, Germany's CPR GmbH, which holds 25.5 percent of shares, and Poland's Stomil Krakgum, which holds the rest.
Szostek said it was not yet clear whether new or existing shares would be issued before the listing of the firm which netted 1.4 million zlotys in 1996 on sales of 13.5 million.
